symptom: `retrieve $Notes from M.Note where [IsOpen = true() and\n\tCount > 0];` is stored as `[IsOpen = true() and Count > 0]` — line break and tab dropped — while split conditions, variable values and member values keep their layout; describe printed any stored constraint on one line, so a Studio Pro layout did not survive describe -> exec into another project.
cause: The visitor kept the source text (SourceExpr); the WRITER dropped it: FormatXPathConstraint sent every constraint containing a line break through the #979 canonical layout, which renders a short one flat. Its doc premise — 'a constraint is rebuilt from its parse tree on every write, so there is no original whitespace left' — had stopped being true once retrieve and access-rule constraints kept their source.
insight: Look at the writer before the visitor: the stored-bytes test (retrieveConstraintOf) showed the visitor's Source intact and the formatter flattening it. The formatter is shared by retrieve, access rule and page datasource, so a write-side change needs the describe side changed for every sink that keeps source (retrieve, grant) or describe -> exec drifts in a new place — the grant round-trip test caught exactly that before it shipped. The rule that keeps both #979 and #1542: a constraint with a line break is the author's layout (kept); a flat one gets the derived layout; describe flattens only text equal to Format(Flatten(x)). Trap when measuring: `create or modify` over the SAME project reports 'Unchanged' with the old build too, because the declared-match compares XPath tokens ignoring whitespace — the drift only shows in a fresh project. Measured on 11.12.1: unfixed stores flat, fixed stores the tab and line break, mx check clean, describe -> exec byte-identical.
